name: Ho Quy Ly
role: Reformer-minister under the late Trần court who seized the throne in 1400, founded the Hồ dynasty and the state of Đại Ngu; lost the country to the Ming invasion of 1406-1407
known_facts: Rose to power as trusted great-minister of Trần Nghệ Tông, who gave him a sword and a flag inscribed 'Văn võ toàn tài, quân thần đồng đức'
Nghệ Tông's blind trust let him kill Trần Phế Đế and clan opponents; in 1400 he deposed the Trần and took the throne, era name Thánh Nguyên, renamed the country Đại Ngu
Within a year passed the throne to his second son Hồ Hán Thương and ruled as thái thượng hoàng, still deciding everything
Militarily weak: as a Trần general he lost repeatedly, was nearly killed by Chăm king Chế Bồng Nga and saved only by Trần Khát Chân
The pretext for invasion came from Trần Thiêm Bình, who fled to the Ming court claiming to be Trần Nghệ Tông's son and begged the Ming to attack
Sept 1406: 200,000 Ming troops under Trương Phụ and Mộc Thạnh invaded; reached the key citadel Đa Bang in four months
Đa Bang fell after his general Nguyễn Tông Đỗ drove war elephants out; Ming fire-arrows and guns spooked the elephants, which fled back into the fort with the Ming following
1407: the Hồ army dissolved at Lỗi Giang and Điển Canh without a real fight; general Ngụy Thức wept and begged the two Hồ to self-immolate rather than be taken
He refused to die with honour, fled to Hà Tĩnh, and he and his sons Hồ Nguyên Trừng and Hồ Hán Thương were captured
A radical reformer 'born in the wrong era': put mathematics into the civil exams, criticised formalist Confucianism, pushed practical study
Promoted chữ Nôm for common teaching and set up free schools at prefectural seats (before, only Thăng Long had public schools)

Set up y tỳ (state medical offices, an early hospital), reformed criminal law and taxes, exempted the landless, widows and orphans, and capped the number of bondservants on aristocratic estates - which struck the Trần nobility
Issued the first paper money in Vietnamese history, holding bronze for military and technical use rather than trade - a 19th-20th century idea in the 15th
Said by the author to be a 15th-century Vietnamese Minh Trị (Meiji), 400 years early, whose reforms were 'a firefly's streak in the desert night' because the age could not follow him
Of Chiết Giang (Chinese) descent by tradition, yet fought the Ming to the end and pushed Vietnamese self-reliance and chữ Nôm - the accusation of leaning to China does not fit his acts
interpretation: Late-Trần / early-Hồ Đại Việt court dress of the turn of the 15th century, based on the user reference.
